text: From the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn they made finely woven garments for ministering in the sanctuary, and they made the holy garments for Aaron, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He made the ephod of gold, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen.
They hammered out sheets of gold and cut them into threads to work into the blue, the purple, the scarlet yarn, and the fine linen—the work of a skilled craftsman.
They made shoulder pieces for the ephod, joined to it at its two edges.

versions.text: They made shoulder pieces for it, joined at its two ends, so that it was held together.
versions.explanation: The current rendering repeats the idea of joining twice ("joined... so that it was held together"), which sounds redundant when read aloud. Naming the ephod also clarifies what "it" refers to after the previous verse.

text: The skillfully woven band on the ephod was of one piece with it and made like it: of gold, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They prepared the onyx stones, mounted in gold filigree settings and engraved like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel.
He fastened them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as stones of remembrance for the sons of Israel, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He made the breastpiece, the work of a skilled craftsman, like the work of the ephod: of gold, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen.
It was square, and they made the breastpiece doubled over—a span long and a span wide, doubled.
They set in it four rows of stones. The first row was carnelian, topaz, and emerald.
The second row was turquoise, sapphire, and diamond.
The third row was jacinth, agate, and amethyst.
The fourth row was beryl, onyx, and jasper. They were mounted in gold filigree settings.
The stones corresponded to the names of the sons of Israel: twelve stones for their twelve names, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes.
For the breastpiece they made braided chains of pure gold, like cords.
They made two gold filigree settings and two gold rings, and fastened the two rings to the two ends of the breastpiece.
They fastened the two gold cords to the two rings at the ends of the breastpiece,
and the other two ends of the cords they fastened to the two settings, attaching them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front.
They made two gold rings and put them at the two ends of the breastpiece, on the inside edge next to the ephod.
They made two more gold rings and attached them to the bottom of the two shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front, close to the seam just above the woven band of the ephod.
They bound the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that it rested on the woven band and would not come loose from the ephod, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He made the robe of the ephod entirely of blue, the work of a weaver,
with an opening in the center of the robe like the opening of a collar, and a binding around the opening so that it would not tear.
On the hem of the robe they made pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, finely twisted.
They made bells of pure gold and attached them between the pomegranates all around the hem of the robe,
alternating a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, all around the hem of the robe for ministering, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
For Aaron and his sons they made tunics of fine linen, the work of a weaver,
and the turban of fine linen, the ornate headbands of fine linen, the linen undergarments of finely twisted linen,
and the sash of finely twisted linen with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, the work of an embroiderer, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold and engraved on it, like an inscription on a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD.
They fastened a blue cord to it to attach it to the turban above, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
So all the work on the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, was completed. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then they brought the tabernacle to Moses: the tent and all its furnishings, its clasps, frames, crossbars, posts, and bases;
the covering of ram skins dyed red, the covering of fine leather, and the shielding curtain;
the ark of the testimony with its poles and the mercy seat;
the table with all its utensils and the bread of the Presence;
the lampstand of pure gold with its lamps set in a row, and all its utensils, and the oil for the light;

versions.text: the lampstand of pure gold with its row of lamps and all its utensils, and the oil for the light;
versions.explanation: The Hebrew names the lamps and then specifies that they are the lamps of the arrangement (row). "Its row of lamps" compresses this and slightly obscures that the lamps themselves are the objects handed over.

text: the gold altar, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the curtain for the entrance to the tent;
the bronze altar with its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils; the basin with its stand;

the curtains of the courtyard with their posts and bases, the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard, its ropes and tent pegs, and all the equipment for the service of the tabernacle, the tent of meeting;

versions.text: the curtains of the courtyard with its posts and bases, the curtain for the entrance to the courtyard, its ropes and tent pegs, and all the equipment for the service of the tabernacle, the tent of meeting;
versions.explanation: "The curtains... with its posts" creates a number mismatch for a listener, since the nearest noun is plural. "Their" reads more naturally while still conveying the courtyard's furnishings.

text: and the finely woven garments for ministering in the sanctuary—the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments for his sons to serve as priests.
Just as the LORD had commanded Moses, so the Israelites did all the work.

versions.text: The Israelites had done all the work just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew places the comparative clause first and repeats it with 'so they did' (כֵּן עָשׂוּ), a rhetorical emphasis lost in the current rendering. Restoring the order preserves the emphasis and reads well aloud.

text: Moses inspected all the work, and there it was—made just as the LORD had commanded; so they had made it. And Moses blessed them.

versions.text: Moses inspected all the work, and saw that they had done it exactly as the LORD had commanded. So Moses blessed them.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew וְהִנֵּה ('and behold') and the emphatic repetition כֵּן עָשׂוּ ('so they did') are both flattened in the current version. Also, 'So Moses blessed them' implies the blessing resulted from the inspection; the Hebrew simply narrates 'and Moses blessed them.'

versions.text: Moses inspected all the work, and there it was—they had done it just as the LORD had commanded; so they had done. And Moses blessed them.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew doubling (עָשׂוּ אֹתָהּ ... כֵּן עָשׂוּ) is rightly preserved, but 'so they had done' without an object leaves the clause dangling in English and stumbles when read aloud. Supplying the object ('so they had made it') keeps the emphatic repetition while producing a complete, speakable clause. Rendering the verb as 'made' also better fits מְלָאכָה (the craftwork of the tabernacle) and distinguishes it from the 'service/work' vocabulary of the preceding verse.
